Content: . . .In `1930`, Gandhi led a `text(240-mile)` march against the British monopoly on salt manufacture. His object was to take the marchers to the sea, to the coastal village of Dandi, Gujarat, where they would illegally extract salt from the seawater. Gandhi set off from the ashram [religious retreat] with a handful of followers, but, as the procession crossed India, more and more people joined the protest, including foreign newspaper reporters and newsreel crews. Reported worldwide, the Salt Campaign brought much support to the cause of Indian independence. Again imprisoned in `1932`, Gandhi fasted for `text(six days)` in protest of the treatment of the untouchables [dalits]. In `1933`, he fasted for `text(twenty-one days)`, an action that secured his release from prison by officials fearful of an insurrection [revolt] if Gandhi should die in custody.
